## Prior art

- [doi:10.37236/41](https://doi.org/10.37236/41) (Paths section, p. 18), checked 2026-10-21: States that sat(n,P\_k) is known for all n when k \<= 6, citing Kaszonyi-Tuza 1986 and Dudek-Wojda 2004; gives no P5 formula itself.
- [https://opuscula.agh.edu.pl/vol24/1/art/opuscula\_math\_2404.pdf](https://opuscula.agh.edu.pl/vol24/1/art/opuscula_math_2404.pdf) (Theorem 2, p. 44), checked 2026-10-21: Opuscula Math. 24(1) (2004) 43-55, restating Kaszonyi-Tuza: sat(n;P5) = n - floor((n-2)/6) - 1 for n \>= 6, which gives 6 at n = 8. No P5 minimum family is stated. Kaszonyi-Tuza 1986 (doi:10.1002/jgt.3190100209) itself was not read (paywalled).
- [https://preview.memphis.edu/msci/people/pbalistr/edge\_spectrum.pdf](https://preview.memphis.edu/msci/people/pbalistr/edge_spectrum.pdf) (Theorem 4(c) (author preprint, March 2018)), checked 2026-10-21: Balister-Dogan, J. Graph Theory 89(4) (2018): for n \>= 5, sat(n;P5) = ceil((5n-4)/6); 6 at n = 8.
- [https://digitalcommons.memphis.edu/speccoll-faudreerj/27](https://digitalcommons.memphis.edu/speccoll-faudreerj/27) (P5 column, table on p. 5), checked 2026-10-21: Lists sat(8,P5) = 6 with graph Y40 with K1; that label was not compared with this witness. Unrefereed technical report (Jambulapati and Faudree, dated 2014-11-18, posted 2021); values for n \<= 9 obtained by exhaustive computer search (p. 3).

## History

P5-free and P5-saturated (re-verified from graph6). A 6-vertex double-star component plus a disjoint edge; degree sequence \[3,3,1,1,1,1,1,1\]. This realizes the plateau sat(8,P5)=sat(7,P5)=6. Deposited 2026-07-14 as HoG #57173.
